 Daylight Saving Time ends November 1
 October 20, 2026 Local Stories 
 We’ll be turning our clocks back an hour on November 1 as Daylight Saving Time ends.
 While some may use that as an excuse to stay up later, Priority Health nurse care manager Charlotte Hobbs says that’s not a great idea.
 “People take that extra hour to stay awake longer instead of keeping that consistent sleep schedule,” Hobbs said. “That’s what’s so important — to keep your internal body clock on a regular schedule. Even on your weekends or days off, it’s really important to go to bed around the same time and to wake up at the same time.”
 Hobbs recommends putting your phone and laptop away at bedtime because that blue light messes up our sleep patterns. She says poor sleep can lead to a risk of heart attack and other health problems.
